steps.description: Stress-test the T1S2 result. caveats: A well-written report can make a confounded result look authoritative; the framing must actively prevent that.
steps.context: The user asked a question the data cannot cleanly answer. The deliverable's value is a correctly-caveated candidate list plus an actionable path to a valid answer, not a confident signature.

constraints: The confounding limitation must appear first in the report, not in a footnote.

Section listing analyses deliberately not attempted, with the reason for each

No claim attributes any gene specifically to treatment rather than batch

plan.title: Treated vs control lung RNA-seq under batch–condition confounding
plan.analytical_narrative:
The dataset is a 12-sample bulk RNA-seq count matrix (12,000 genes x 12 samples, salmon gene-level integer counts, gene symbols in column 1) with metadata giving condition (6 treated, 6 control) and batch (B1 = all controls, B2 = all treated). Batch is PERFECTLY confounded with condition: no statistical procedure can separate a treatment effect from a B1-vs-B2 processing effect in these data. This constraint dictates the whole plan.

T1S1 runs QC and an unsupervised structure assessment (library sizes, detection rates, filtering, VST/CPM, PCA, sample correlation heatmap, hierarchical clustering) and — critically — formally documents the confounding by showing the condition and batch design matrices are rank-deficient when combined, so any downstream 'treatment' estimate is really a 'treatment+batch' estimate. T1S2 runs the only estimable contrast, treated vs control, with a negative-binomial GLM on raw counts (DESeq2 preferred; edgeR/limma-voom or pydeseq2 as fallbacks, probed at run time since the package inventory could not be read), reporting shrunken log2FC, BH-FDR, and labelling every result as a confounded treatment+batch effect. It explicitly does NOT attempt batch correction: removing batch removes the condition effect, and applying ComBat/limma removeBatchEffect here would silently null the contrast or produce anticonservative p-values. T1S3 probes robustness — does the gene list depend on the DE engine, on filtering, on one sample? — and checks whether the DE signature looks like a technical batch signature (global shift, GC/length-agnostic proxies such as mitochondrial/ribosomal/housekeeping gene behaviour, fraction of genome moving) versus a focused biological response. That distinction is the only leverage available for judging plausibility without new samples.

T2S1 takes the ranked gene list into pathway/GSEA-style enrichment purely as hypothesis generation. No reference store is provisioned right now, so the step must first check for gene sets in the environment and, if none exist, report that enrichment could not be run rather than inventing gene sets — the core research question survives without it. T2S2 writes the honest synthesis: the effect estimate, its confounded interpretation, what would be needed to break the confound (samples of both conditions in at least one shared batch, or technical replicates bridging B1 and B2), and an explicit statement that no gene here can be attributed to treatment as opposed to processing batch. Resources are small throughout: the matrix is ~12,000 x 12 and fits comfortably in 2–4 GB.

steps.context: The user asked a question the data cannot cleanly answer. The deliverable's value is a correctly-caveated candidate list plus an actionable path to a valid answer, not a confident signature.
constraints: The confounding limitation must appear first in the report, not in a footnote.
Do not describe any gene as a treatment-responsive gene without the treatment-or-batch qualifier.
Quantitative claims must trace back to numbers produced in T1S1-T2S1; do not introduce new estimates in the report.
If T2S1 reported missing gene sets, say so in the report rather than omitting enrichment silently.
acceptance_criteria: Report opens with the batch-condition aliasing and its consequence for interpretation
Ranked candidate gene list with log2FC, FDR, and stability annotation is included
Section listing analyses deliberately not attempted, with the reason for each
Concrete remediation options for breaking the confound, including bridge/shared-batch designs and independent validation
No claim attributes any gene specifically to treatment rather than batch
caveats: A well-written report can make a confounded result look authoritative; the framing must actively prevent that.
